summary: Four new payloads for any order — the turn in flight, the full anatomy of every finished turn including tool parameters and subagents, the context window's composition and delta, and a diagnosis saying why an order is not moving — each with a rendered CLI command and all four on one dashboard debugging view; then a tool that clears the blocker the diagnosis named through the remedies that already ship, and a gate and meter retrofitted over the lot so debugging is configurable and its own cost is visible in the bill. OTEL is decided by measurement.

children.title: jarvis watch: the turn in flight, read from the transcript
children.description: New file src/jarvis/live.py, one function in ops.py, one command in cli.py. Do NOT touch inspection.py, usage.py, bill.py, any route or any template: a sibling is rewriting the walk inside inspection.read_transcript and you would conflict. Own tests/test_live.py; no sibling adds to it. Copy the row builders stamp/prompt_row/assistant_row/tool_rows out of tests/test_inspection.py INTO your own file rather than importing or moving them — that file belongs to the sibling building subagent anatomy. The dashboard page that renders your payload is a separate, later work order.
children.acceptance: tests/test_live.py, fabricating the session by hand (monkeypatch usage.TRANSCRIPT_ROOT_ENV to a tmp dir, write <tmp>/-proj/<session>.jsonl, attach with UPDATE work_orders SET session_id). Prove: (1) a trailing tool_use with no matching tool_result, stamped seconds ago, returns now['tool'] with elapsed > 0 and state 'working'; (2) appending rows and re-reading from the returned cursor parses only the appended bytes, while rewriting the file with a different first line restarts from offset 0 — the uilog.read_errors contract; (3) cli.main(['watch', wo_id, '--once', '--json']) parses to the same dict as ops.live_report. ABSENT IS NOT ZERO: no session_id, and a missing transcript file, each give found False / state 'no-transcript' / turn None / now None, with an explicit assertion that no 0 or 0.0 is presented as a reading; a transcript whose last row is minutes old gives state 'generating' with a real stale_seconds and a note saying nothing has been written since that timestamp. Leave tests/test_inspection.py, tests/test_usage.py and tests/test_cost_report.py green and untouched. The repaint loop and --interval are a hand check with a screenshot in the PR, not a test.

children.title: Tool parameters and subagent sessions in the turn anatomy
children.description: You own src/jarvis/inspection.py and tests/test_inspection.py exclusively; no sibling edits either file. Outside them, touch only cli._print_anatomy and its parser wiring. Do NOT create src/jarvis/live.py and do NOT read a running session — a sibling owns live reading, in that new module, precisely so the two of you never edit the same walk. Do not touch usage.py pricing, bill.py, ops.py, any route or any template. The dashboard renderer of your payload is a separate, later work order and it depends on you, so grow keys and change none.
children.acceptance: tests/test_inspection.py, using its existing write_transcript fixture, which already accepts subagents={'agent-x': [rows]}. Prove: (1) a 100kB tool input comes back truncated with the cap stated in the payload the way Anatomy.as_dict already states write_floor and join_floor, and the untruncated value never appears; (2) redaction is a NAMED function with its own direct unit tests — a token-like string, a file body, a Bash command carrying a secret — plus a test proving the payload path calls it rather than an inline regex; (3) a synthetic subagent's tokens and tool calls appear under the parent turn AND are a partition: the parent turn's own totals are unchanged by attaching it; (4) the payload names the nesting depth actually read, and a subagent-of-a-subagent that cannot be reached is reported as unreached, not as none. Every number pinned against the committed real session stays exact: 1886/576/58, [(865,136,26),(885,440,23),(136,0,9)], cache_5m 569173, context_peak 233585, 55 Bash calls. cli.PART_LABELS must still equal inspection.PARTS. SUBAGENT WRITES: a synthetic subagent carrying a cache write has that write classified by inspection.classify_writes as the SUBAGENT's own and never folded into the parent's classification, with its own context_peak reported; assert the parent's classification is unchanged by attaching it. CLI IS THE PRIMARY SURFACE: cli._print_anatomy renders the tool parameters and the subagent rows as text a person reads, screenshotted in the PR, with a test asserting the rendered output contains the parameter summary and the subagent label.

children.title: The context ledger: what Jarvis put in the window, and the delta
children.description: New file src/jarvis/context.py, one write call in dispatch.py, one column in ProjectStore's ADDED_COLUMNS, ops.context_report, and a `jarvis wo context` command. Own tests/test_context.py; append ONE test to tests/test_schema_upgrade.py beside policy's. Write unconditionally: a later sibling retrofits the level guard, so do not anticipate it. Do NOT edit inspection.classify_writes or invariants.check_prefix_stable: you read both and change neither. Your measurement must not alter the prompt text dispatch.build_worker_prompt produces, nor the value of hooks.prefix_fingerprint.
children.acceptance: Two files, because the schema rule needs two halves. In tests/test_context.py: dispatch under fake_claude, read the column back through ProjectStore, assert the ingredient list round-trips. In tests/test_schema_upgrade.py: build today's schema, ALTER TABLE wo_turns DROP COLUMN to age it one release, reopen with ProjectStore, assert the column is back AND a turn created on the upgraded database round-trips a payload. Do NOT use tests/data/schema-jarvis-0.1.11.sql — it predates wo_turns entirely, so it would pass with the ADDED_COLUMNS entry forgotten. ABSENT IS NOT ZERO: an order whose turns all predate the column renders the literal note 'not recorded for this order' — assert that string, not an empty list. Assert the residual row is labelled measured false and that no ingredient claims a byte-exact rendered system prompt. Assert prefix_break defers: where the delta and classify_writes disagree, the write classification is reported as the authority and the delta as the hypothesis, and no new alarm is raised. Leave tests/test_schema_upgrade.py, test_pipeline.py, test_worker_brief.py and test_stable_prefix.py green. SUBAGENTS ARE NOT YOURS: per-subagent context composition is out of reach because Jarvis does not build a subagent's prompt; the payload must say so in words and point at the anatomy surface for a subagent's tokens, writes and context peak — assert that string. CLI IS THE PRIMARY SURFACE: `jarvis wo context` renders the ingredients with each one's share of the window and the delta from the previous turn as a table a person reads, screenshotted in the PR, with a test asserting the rendered output names each ingredient and the residual.

children.title: jarvis wo why: why this order is not moving, and what to type
children.description: ops.diagnose plus a `jarvis wo why` command. You compose existing functions and rewrite none: ops.waiting_on, invariants.true_blockers / parked_reason / pause_note / fleet_hold_note / status_label, holds.held and agent_usage are read-only to you, and a diagnosis that disagrees with the status label is worse than none. Own tests/test_wo_why.py; no sibling adds to it. Do NOT call ops.live_report — a sibling owns it and it will not exist while you build; your clock comes from the store. Do NOT touch remedies.py or any acting path. No dashboard route.
children.acceptance: tests/test_wo_why.py, building each state with the existing fixtures the way tests/test_resume_auto_diagnosis.py does: pending assumption, escalated gate, gate with Neo, held-and-unargued gate, Neo question, queued message, running turn, settled order. Prove: (1) for each state the report's blocker equals what ops.waiting_on returns for the same store and work order — no second opinion; (2) where two sources disagree, BOTH appear in the payload and a field says they disagree, with a test constructing such a case; (3) a failed agent_usage row for the order is described as UNREACHABLE, with an assertion that the words decided, escalated and refused do not appear for it; (4) the offered commands are only ones the OS would accept right now — no `jarvis validation force` on a running order, no `jarvis wo ack` on one with pending assumptions; (5) cli.main(['wo','why',wo_id,'--json']) parses to the same dict. READ-ONLY: assert ops.diagnose leaves store.list_events(wo_id) unchanged. With no live session the clock marks the reading unavailable rather than reporting 0. Anatomy.unexplained prints as a residual, never as a cause. CLI IS THE PRIMARY SURFACE: `jarvis wo why` renders the blocker, how long it has been there and the command that clears it as text, screenshotted in the PR, with a test asserting the rendered output contains the command it offers.

children.title: The debugging view: one dashboard page for all four payloads
children.description: Two routes in src/jarvis/ui/app.py beside the existing work_order route, new templates, the cross-links to and from /cost, and one line in `jarvis cost` naming the three new commands. You render four ops functions verbatim and compute nothing. Own tests/test_ui_debug.py; no sibling adds to it. Do NOT edit src/jarvis/live.py, src/jarvis/inspection.py, src/jarvis/context.py or ops.diagnose — four siblings own those and all four have landed before you start. Do not change bill.py or /cost; the observability cost class is already in the bill from policy.
children.acceptance: tests/test_ui_debug.py with fastapi's TestClient, copying the client fixture from tests/test_ui_cost.py. Do NOT put the proof in tests_browser/ — Playwright runs as a separate CI job needing `playwright install chromium` and is not in the default testpaths; a test there is optional extra, never the evidence. Prove: (1) the page is 200 and the diagnosis block appears BEFORE the live block in page.text, using the index-comparison idiom already in tests/test_ui_cost.py; (2) the live JSON route returns exactly ops.live_report's dict, compared against a direct call, proving the route computes nothing; (3) DEGRADATION — monkeypatch each of ops.live_report, ops.inspect_report, ops.context_report and ops.diagnose in turn to raise, and assert the page still returns 200 with the other three blocks rendered and a named note for the failed one; a 500 here reaches the inbox and trips INV-UI-HEALTHY; (4) the debug page and /cost link to each other. Add a test that ?debug=1 on the existing work-order route still means debug-level timeline events. Leave tests/test_ui.py, test_ui_cost.py and test_ui_observability.py green. The poll refreshing is a hand check with a screenshot in the PR.

children.title: jarvis wo fix: clear the blocker the diagnosis named, through the remedies that already ship
children.description: ops.fix, a `jarvis wo fix` command, and one control on the debug page the debug-view sibling landed. You add NO remedy: remedies.REMEDIES is a closed registry and tuple(REMEDIES) == SHIPPED_REMEDIES is asserted, so leave it, RemedyConfig's empty default allow-list and the self_heal grant path through gates.open_gate exactly as they are. You add an ENTRY POINT to nudge, unblock and file_work_order and nothing else. Inherit every exclusion in remedies.py verbatim: no cancelling a turn, no set_status, no wo done, no fo resume, no killing a process. Own tests/test_wo_fix.py.
children.acceptance: tests/test_wo_fix.py, building blockers with the fixtures tests/test_resume_auto_diagnosis.py uses. Prove: (1) for each blocker type a shipped remedy covers, the remedy proposed is the one ops.diagnose named for the same store and work order — no second opinion; (2) a blocker no shipped remedy covers returns section 6's pre-validated command labelled as the user's own to run, never a no-op and never an invented remedy; (3) with RemedyConfig off, or with no approved unspent self_heal grant, it refuses and names which of the two stopped it; (4) an order with no blocker says so and offers nothing, rather than presenting an empty list as nothing to do. REGRESSION, and these are the guard rails: the AST walk in tests/test_remedies.py still passes with every acting call inside a handler, and tuple(remedies.REMEDIES) == remedies.SHIPPED_REMEDIES still asserts. CLI IS THE PRIMARY SURFACE: with no --json the command prints the blocker, the remedy it would propose and the approval that remedy needs, screenshotted in the PR; --json parses to the same dict. Leave tests/test_remedies.py, test_supervisor.py and test_wo_why.py green.

children.title: The observability gate and meter: config precedence and the bill's third class
children.description: New src/jarvis/observability.py holds TWO separate things; never conflate them. The GATE: an ObservabilityConfig on both config dataclasses in catalog.py, a nullable work_orders column, precedence order then project then fleet, default normal. It governs exactly one write, the per-turn ingredient row the context sibling landed, and 'off' stops that row and nothing else. The METER: new agent_usage kinds recording every observability call, the four reads included, never switchable off, plus the class label bill.py needs. Change no bill arithmetic, no route, no template, no payload.
children.acceptance: tests/test_observability.py plus ONE appended test in the shared tests/test_schema_upgrade.py. Prove precedence as a table — order column set, project set, fleet only, nothing set — including that NULL in the column resolves to the project or fleet answer and is NOT 'off'. Prove 'off' stops the per-turn ingredient row and changes no other surface, that the gate is never consulted on any read path while the meter still records those reads, and that all four report functions are wrapped — enumerate them in the test so a forgotten one fails rather than silently under-reports. Prove the dashboard page is metered too with no edit to its routes, since it calls the same ops functions. Prove a failing agent_usage write leaves the measured callable's return value unchanged and raises nothing (monkeypatch the recorder to raise). Prove the meter records wall clock and ZERO tokens for a callable that makes no model call, and that bill.build surfaces those rows as their own class rather than folding them into Jarvis's overhead, asserted against a synthetic agent_usage row in the fixture style of tests/test_cost_report.py. ABSENT IS NOT ZERO: an order with no observability rows renders the literal 'not recorded' — assert that string, never 0.00. In tests/test_schema_upgrade.py: drop the new column to age the database one release, reopen with ProjectStore, assert it is back AND that a work order created on the upgraded database round-trips a level. Leave tests/test_cost_report.py, test_config.py, test_catalog.py and test_schema_upgrade.py green.

children.title: Spike: measure what Claude Code's OTEL export actually emits
children.description: A measurement and a finding, not a feature. Write NO production code: the deliverable is a findings document under docs/specs/, one `jarvis learn add` entry, and a PR carrying both. Touch no module under src/jarvis/ — env vars around a scratch `claude` invocation in your shell suffice. You own the DECISION — adopt, decline or adopt in part — and write it into section 8, the only outside prose any child may edit, in the same PR. If OTEL turns out to add something, file a separate feature order rather than build it here.
children.acceptance: All six questions in the section answered with what arrived or with the word 'nothing', each backed by a recorded payload you can quote — metric and log-event names enumerated; whether tool parameters, cache-write cause / TTL split, and context composition arrive; the flush interval and whether anything arrives from a turn killed mid-flight; the process, port and failure-mode cost under concurrent headless workers. A DECLINE IS AS FULL A SUCCESS AS AN ADOPTION — no recommendation is owed in either direction and none should be manufactured. Read scripts/spike_peer_message.py first; it is this repository's precedent for how a spike is written up. The decision is written into section 8 in the same PR: on a decline, an entry citing this measurement and striking whichever of the four reasons it contradicts; on adopt or adopt in part, one line saying OTEL left this feature for a named follow-on feature order, with its id. One session; if the measurement is incomplete, report what was measured and what was not rather than extending. `uv run pytest tests/ evals/` stays green — which it will, since nothing under src/jarvis/ changed.
